vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: feed-diet
Version: 0.2.0

The OpenClaw AgentSkill 'feed-diet' is classified as benign. The skill's code demonstrates good security practices, notably in `scripts/opml-parse.sh` which explicitly validates RSS feed URLs to prevent Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) by restricting fetches to only `http://` and `https://` schemes. User-provided inputs (like HN usernames or OPML file paths) are handled carefully in shell commands, using double-quoting and passing data to `python3` or `jq` for safe parsing, which mitigates direct shell injection risks. While the `scripts/classify.sh` component constructs prompts for external LLMs using user-provided content (titles, URLs), posing a potential prompt injection vulnerability against the LLM itself, the skill's code attempts to constrain LLM output and strictly parses the results, limiting the impact on the agent's security or system integrity. There is no evidence of intentional harmful behavior such as data exfiltration, backdoors, or unauthorized remote control.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and optional environment usage are consistent with an HN/RSS feed auditing tool — nothing requested or installed is disproportionate to that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (HN + OPML/RSS audit, classification, reports) match the included scripts (hn-fetch.sh, opml-parse.sh, classify.sh, feed-diet.sh). No unrelated credentials, binaries, or installs are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions ask the agent to read either a local OPML path or an HN username and to run the included scripts. The scripts legitimately read local OPML files and fetch remote feed/ HN endpoints and then (optionally) send content to an LLM for classification. This is expected for the stated purpose, but be aware that feed item titles/URLs are sent to external LLMs if you set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with bundled scripts). No URLs that download arbitrary archives; everything is supplied as local shell/python scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required credentials are declared. Two optional env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY) are used only for LLM classification, which is proportional to the classifier feature. The scripts will use these keys to call external LLM APIs when present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable. The skill creates a cache directory under the user's XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache/feed-diet and temporary files — reasonable for local caching. It does not request system-wide privileges or modify other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Feed Diet appears to be what it claims: a local shell-based HN/RSS auditor. Before installing or running it, consider: 1) OPML/feeds you supply will be fetched by the skill — a malicious or internal URL in your OPML could cause the tool to contact internal services (the script allows only http/https but does not restrict hosts). Review OPML contents before use. 2) If you set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY for better classification, titles and URLs from your feeds will be sent to those external providers; don't set keys if you want to keep items local. 3) The skill writes cache files to ~/.cache/feed-diet and uses temporary files — check and rotate/clean as needed. If you plan to run this in a multi-tenant or sensitive environment, review the scripts yourself (they are included) or run them in an isolated environment.
